raw_case_text: Laboratory tests such as complete blood count revealed a white blood cells (WBCs) count of 26,900/muL, 90.9% of them were neutrophils. They also showed elevated inflammatory markers; C-reactive protein (CRP) was 71.3, and later erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) test was 60 mm/h. His other tests which included liver and renal function tests, electrolytes, and urine examination were all within normal limits. MRI study of the entire spine with gadolinium contrast provided evidence of T2 hyperintense signal changes at the level of (10-11-12) thoracic vertebrae, often related to an inflammatory process with no compressive lesion (Figure 1), so electromyography (EMG) was not performed. The patient was managed with short courses of intravenous (IV) antibiotic methylprednisolone solumedrol for 5 days, but he did not get better. During that time we continued with testing the CSF which was turbid with WBCs count of 30/muL, 95% of them are neutrophils with 2760 RBCs, glucose of 63 mg/dL, elevated levels of protein about 67 mg/dL, and immunoglobulin G (IGg) value in the CSF of 5.22 mg/dL with normal CSF IgG Index. There are no malignant cells detected in the examined CSF sample. Computed tomography (CT) of the chest excluded the tuberculosis (TB) infection and when (GeneXpert) PCR in the CSF was performed, it was negative. Immunology tests of anti-aquaporin-4 (APQ-4)-IgG autoantibodies and anti-myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG) autoantibodies were negative. Electrophoresis showed positive oligoclonal bands correlated with systemic inflammation. The patient mentioned a history of unpasteurized dairy products so a real-time PCR for brucella bacteria was performed and it was positive, while it is not usual for brucella bacteria to cause transverse myelitis. We were not able to identify the brucella type because that is not available in our country. The patient opted to transfer his care to another hospital, where the medical team considered the potential benefit of plasmapheresis. However, the intervention proved ineffective due to the advanced disease stage. At that time the patient was commenced on a 6-week course of doxycycline 100 mg twice daily and rifampicin 600 mg once daily, alongside an intensive physical therapy program aimed at optimizing good outcomes.

subjective.past_medical_history: Epidemiological exposure: History of consuming unpasteurized dairy products. No other prior medical history, chronic conditions, or prior medications documented.

objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count: white blood cells (WBC) 26,900/muL (90.9% neutrophils); C-reactive protein (CRP): 71.3; erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR): 60 mm/h. Liver function tests, renal function tests, serum electrolytes, and urinalysis: all within normal limits.
objective.advanced_workup: Spinal MRI with gadolinium contrast demonstrated T2 hyperintense signal changes at the level of T10-T12 thoracic vertebrae suggestive of an inflammatory process without compressive lesion; EMG was not performed. Chest CT excluded pulmonary tuberculosis. Lumbar puncture / CSF analysis: turbid CSF, WBC count 30/muL (95% neutrophils), RBC 2,760/muL, glucose 63 mg/dL, protein 67 mg/dL, CSF IgG 5.22 mg/dL with normal CSF IgG index; cytology negative for malignant cells; CSF GeneXpert PCR for Mycobacterium tuberculosis was negative. Autoantibody testing: anti-aquaporin-4 (AQP-4)-IgG and anti-myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG) autoantibodies negative; protein electrophoresis showed positive oligoclonal bands.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmation: Real-time PCR for Brucella bacteria was positive (specific species typing unavailable locally), establishing Brucella-induced transverse myelitis. Differential diagnoses ruled out: Compressive myelopathy excluded by spine MRI; tuberculosis excluded by chest CT and negative CSF GeneXpert PCR; neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) and MOGAD excluded by negative anti-AQP-4 and anti-MOG antibodies; malignancy ruled out by CSF cytology. Management and Outcome: Initially treated with short courses of IV antibiotics and methylprednisolone (Solu-Medrol) for 5 days without improvement. Plasmapheresis was considered and attempted at a transfer facility but was ineffective due to advanced disease stage. The patient was then treated with a 6-week course of oral doxycycline 100 mg twice daily and oral rifampicin 600 mg once daily, combined with intensive physical therapy.
